program_description: 12-week kettlebell + running program. Intermediate. Fat loss + muscle gain. 5 training days, 6 sessions/week (one two-a-day).

sarge.name: Sarge
sarge.personality: Grizzled veteran. Ex-Force Recon. Dry humor, no compliments wasted. Calls you 'son' when warm, 'boot' when sharp.
voice_traits: no exclamation points unless quoting orders
signature_phrases: Pain is information. Listen to it. Don't obey it.
The body's lying. The bell ain't.

kai.name: Kai
kai.personality: Sharp older brother. Former D1 athlete, hybrid trainer. Fast, witty, sarcastic with affection. Will roast you for half-reps.
voice_traits: calls you by your first name or 'big dog'
signature_phrases: That was three reps. I counted. Don't make me count again.
If you can text right now, you're not working.
Pretty form is fast form. Ugly form gets you hurt.
We're not done. We're just between sets.

marcus.name: Marcus
marcus.personality: Stoic philosopher-coach. Ex-monk turned movement specialist. Quiet, deliberate, grounded. Drops a quote without preamble. Fire when needed.
voice_traits: occasional Marcus Aurelius or Epictetus reference
never raises voice but commands attention
signature_phrases: Breath first. The body follows breath.
You're rushing. The bell will wait.
What stands in the way becomes the way.
Slow is smooth. Smooth is strong.
This rep is the only one that exists.

energy_substitution_rules.description: Start-of-workout energy reading (1-10) substitutes coach lines and may adjust load.

low_energy.behavior: Coach softens tone, acknowledges low energy, may suggest -10% load or -1 round. Marcus leans heavier into breath work. Sarge becomes 'show up anyway' mode (no jokes about it). Kai drops the sarcasm and switches to encouragement.

high_energy.behavior: Coach sharpens. Sarge gets stricter on form. Kai turns up the roast. Marcus challenges you to add 1 rep per set. Optional load bump +5lb on main lifts.

mid_workout_checkin_rules.description: Triggered roughly halfway through workout. Three options for user: 'light' / 'right' / 'heavy'.

light.behavior: Coach challenges to up tempo or reps for remaining sets. Sarge: 'Then you're lying or your bell is. Pick.' Kai: 'Cool, we're adding two reps per set. You're welcome.' Marcus: 'Then deepen the breath and find the next gear.'

right.behavior: Coach affirms briefly and pushes forward. Sarge: 'Copy.' Kai: 'Stay in the pocket.' Marcus: 'This is the place.'

heavy.behavior: Coach offers options: reduce load 10%, drop a round, or extend rest by 30s. Sarge: 'Pull back ten percent. Finish standing.' Kai: 'Drop a round. Better to do four clean than five sloppy.' Marcus: 'Add thirty seconds rest. The work waits for you.'

weeks.theme: Re-introduce the patterns. Build the floor.

blocks.narration: Alright, son. First day. I'm not going to ask if you're ready because the answer is always yes. You showed up. That's the first rep. Twenty-five minutes. We're keeping it clean. Foundation week. The bell you grab today is the one you can move with intent. Not ego. Intent. Let's move.

Three minutes of warm-up. Halos first. Slow circles around the head. Don't shrug your shoulders to your ears. Then goblet squat to stand. Eight of them. Sit between your heels. Last is the hinge. Ten reps. Hands on your hip crease. Push your butt back like you're closing a car door with it. That's the swing pattern. Memorize it.

movements.name: Two-hand swing
movements.cue: Hike the bell back. Snap the hips. Stand tall. The bell floats. You don't lift it.

movements.name: Goblet squat
movements.cue: Elbows inside the knees at the bottom. Drive through the floor.

movements.name: Strict press (right)
movements.cue: Pack the shoulder. Don't lean back. Press, don't push.

movements.name: Strict press (left)
movements.cue: Same as the other side. Both shoulders earn their keep.

movements.name: Bent-over row (right)
movements.cue: Flat back. Pull the bell to your hip, not your chest.

movements.name: Bent-over row (left)
movements.cue: Same again. Squeeze the shoulder blade at the top.

narration_per_round: Round one. We're greasing the groove. Move like you've got nothing to prove. Because today, you don't.
Round two. Same movements. Better positions. The first round was the rehearsal. This one's the take.
Last round. You've got it now. Don't speed up just because the end is in sight. Finish the way you started.

blocks.narration: Two minutes. Fifteen swings at the top of each minute. Whatever time is left, you rest. If you finish the swings in twenty seconds, you get forty seconds of rest. If you take fifty, you get ten. Math doesn't care about your feelings. Move.

That's the work, son. Twenty-five minutes. Day one. You don't get a medal for this. You get a rep on the calendar. The medal comes at week twelve. Rate the session honest. The data only helps if you don't lie to it. Dismissed.

Good. You came back. The second workout is harder than the first because nothing forced you here except the version of yourself you're trying to build. Today is the Turkish get-up. We will not rush. We will not load heavy. The get-up is a conversation between every joint in your body. Listen to it.

Four minutes. Move slowly. The body is a stiff hinge in the morning of a session. Open the spine. Open the hips. Walk through one get-up with no weight first. You should know where every limb is going before you add iron.

movements.name: Turkish get-up
movements.cue: Eyes on the bell on the way up. Eyes forward on the way down. Don't rush the transitions. Every position is a checkpoint.

narration_per_round: Minute one. Right side. Press the bell. Lock the elbow. Roll to the elbow. The bell stays vertical. Always.
Minute two. Left side. The body remembers asymmetries. We're balancing the ledger.
Three. Right. By now you should feel the obliques engage on the sit-up. If you don't, slow it down.
Five. Right. Halfway. Marcus Aurelius wrote that we should perform every action as if it were our last. Try that with this rep.
Six. Left. Last side of the front half. Feel your shoulder pack. It's listening.
Seven. Right. The back half is where most people get sloppy. You won't.
Eight. Left. The descent matters more than the ascent. Most injuries happen on the way down. Reverse the order. Slowly.
Nine. Right. Second to last on this side. Make it the cleanest one yet.
Ten. Left. Final rep. End with control. The set isn't done until the bell is back on the floor.

movements.name: Halo + goblet squat flow
movements.reps: 1 halo each way + 1 squat = 1 rep. AMRAP 3 min.

blocks.narration: Three-minute flow. Halo right, halo left, one squat. That's one rep. Move continuously. Breathe through the nose if you can. This is the bridge between work and rest. The work isn't over but the urgency is.

That's the session. Twenty-five minutes. You worked one movement and one finisher and that was enough. The get-up will teach you more than any other lift over the next twelve weeks if you let it. Rate the work honestly. Tomorrow is Kai. He talks more than I do. Don't say I didn't warn you.

Alright, big dog. Kai's up. Sarge had you grinding, Marcus had you meditating, now we're playing a different game. Twenty-five minutes. A complex. Five movements stitched together, no setting the bell down. You're going to feel your heart rate. That's the point. Don't fight it. Date it.

Four minutes warm-up. Jacks first. Don't half-rep them, I'll know. Inchworms next, five of those. Squat ten times, get the knees over the toes a little, it's fine, the internet lied to you about that. Arm circles last. Wake up the shoulders. Let's go.

blocks.structure: 4 rounds of the complex. Rest 90s between rounds. Same bell throughout.
narration_per_round: Round one. Take it cool. You're learning the pattern. Don't race. Move from one to the next like you've done it a thousand times, even if you haven't.
Round two. The bell got heavier. Yes I know. No I don't care. Same numbers. Go.
Round three. Halfway through your halfway. We've passed the point where it's a warm-up and we're squarely in the part where you decide what kind of guy you are.
Last round. Last round. Whatever you held back, spend it. The bell goes down empty.

blocks.narration: Two minutes on the rope. Doesn't matter if you trip. Just don't quit. Find a rhythm. If you can't go straight through, do thirty on, ten off, thirty on, until time's up. Get the heart rate up one more time then we're done.

Done. Twenty-five minutes. You moved a bell about a thousand pounds total volume today. Not bad for a Wednesday. Rate it honest, big dog. Tomorrow is rest day. Real rest. Don't sneak a workout in. Recovery is where the gains live.

Double day. Don't get cute about it, we're easing in. Run first. Twenty minutes. Six minutes easy warm-up, then six rounds of thirty seconds hard, thirty seconds easy. That's three minutes of work, three of recovery, then jog home. Welcome to intervals.
Six minutes easy. Conversational pace. If you can't talk, you're going too hard. We haven't started yet.

narration_per_round: Round one. Hard means hard, not flat-out. You'd hit a wall by round four. Pace it.
Three. Halfway. This is where you find out if your warm-up was honest.
Four. Three to go. The legs are heavier now. Welcome to the club.
Five. Almost. Don't shorten your stride. Keep the form.
Six. Last hard one. Empty it.

blocks.narration: Eight minutes easy jog home. Should feel like you're floating compared to the intervals. Get the heart rate back down before the KB session. Hydrate.

Second session. The bell. Twenty minutes. You've got some fatigue from the run, that's the point. Welcome to the hybrid life. We're keeping it simple. Three movements, four rounds. Press, swing, squat. Move, rest, repeat.

narration_per_round: Round one. Right arm press. The legs are tired, the shoulders aren't. Take advantage.
Two. Left arm. Same notes. Keep the form even if you have to slow down.
Three. Right again. We alternate every round so both shoulders get equal love. And equal hate.

blocks.narration: That's the double. Forty-five total minutes today. You earned the weekend. Marcus has you on Saturday for the long run. He's gonna make it feel like meditation. Don't be fooled. It still hurts.

Thirty minutes. Easy pace. The kind of pace where you could speak in full sentences if you had to. This is not a hard run. This is the run that teaches the body how to use fat as fuel. It looks easy and it works on you anyway. That is the design.

narration_segments.narration: Begin. Find the breath first. In through the nose, out through the mouth. If you can't breathe through your nose, you're too fast. Slow down until you can.
Five minutes in. The first five are always the hardest. The body protests. Then it remembers. Let it remember.
Ten. A third of the way through. Notice where your jaw is. If it's clenched, unclench it. Tension in the face is wasted energy.
Halfway. Epictetus wrote that no man is free who is not master of himself. The slow pace is harder than the fast one for men who do not yet master themselves. You are practicing the harder thing.
Twenty. Two-thirds. The mind will start to wander now. Let it. But every few minutes, return to the breath. The mind goes where the breath leads it back.
Five minutes left. Don't speed up yet. The discipline is to finish at the pace you started.
One minute. Hold the pace. The temptation to sprint the end is ego. We don't feed ego today.

blocks.narration: Thirty minutes. Done. You did not race anyone, including yourself. That is a kind of strength most men never learn. Rate the session. Then drink water. Then rest. Tomorrow is Sarge.

Week one. Last session. Thirty minutes. The grind. We're going to do one thing, mostly. Swings. A lot of them. Spread across thirty minutes. You're going to want to rush. Don't. We're building an engine. Engines are built slow.
Four minutes. Same warm-up as Monday but with a light swing set at the end. Get the hinge feeling crisp before you go heavy.

blocks.structure: EMOM x 20. 10 two-hand swings at the top of every minute.

movements.name: Two-hand swing
movements.cue: Hike. Snap. Stand. The bell is light. The volume is what cooks you. Don't grip too hard. Save the forearms.

narration_per_round: Minute one. Ten swings. Easy. You've got fifty seconds to rest. Use it.
Two. Ten more. Same numbers, same form.
Three. Now we're warming up the engine.
Four. Two hundred pounds of swing volume in. Eighteen hundred to go.
Five. A quarter. Settle in. You've got time.
Six. The forearms are talking. Tell them to wait their turn.
Eight. Almost halfway. The middle is where men either find the rhythm or quit. Find the rhythm.
Ten. Halfway. Take a breath at the top of the next minute before you start. One breath. Not five.
Twelve. The bell is the same weight. You're heavier now. That's training.
Fourteen. The last six are the only ones that build the engine. Everything before this was the cost of entry.
Eighteen. Three left. The bell didn't get heavier. Your grip did. Squeeze on the swing, relax at the bottom.
Twenty. Last minute. Ten clean ones. Finish the way you started, son.

blocks.narration: Two hundred swings. Two hundred clean swings on day seven of twelve weeks. That's the work. Rest tomorrow. Drink water. Don't be a hero with your diet today, eat enough to recover. Week two starts Monday. I'll see you then.

weeks.theme: Add reps. Tighten form. Same patterns, more volume.

blocks.narration: Week two. You came back. Good. Most don't. We're adding a round and a few reps this week. The patterns are the same. The volume creeps. That's how foundation works. Bone first, then muscle on top. Twenty-seven minutes. Let's go.
Three minutes. Same warm-up, two more reps on the squat and hinge. Wake the hips up. They're going to work today.

movements.name: Two-hand swing
movements.cue: Hike high. Snap hard. The bell floats.

movements.name: Goblet squat
movements.cue: Pause one second at the bottom each rep. Earn the stand-up.

narration_per_round: Round one. Same as last week but cleaner. Last week was rehearsal. This week we're on stage.
Two. The squat has a pause now. Don't skip it. The pause is where the strength gets built.
Three. You felt the extra round before you felt it. Now you're in it. Stay calm.
Last round. The fourth round of anything is where character shows up. Show it.

blocks.narration: Three minutes. Fifteen swings at the top of each minute. Same drill as last week, one more round. The math is simple. The work isn't.
Day eight in the books. You added one round, ten reps of swings, and a pause on every squat. That is what week two looks like. Rate it. Tomorrow Marcus. Get-up volume goes up too. Heads up.

Twelve get-ups today. Six each side. The bell is the same. The volume is more. You will be tempted to rush the last few. Do not. The last get-up matters more than the first because fatigue is when form fails. Form is what we are building.
Four minutes. We added bird dogs today. They wake up the cross-body connection that the get-up depends on. Move slowly.

movements.name: Turkish get-up
movements.cue: Same cues as last week. Eyes on the bell going up. Eyes forward coming down. Vertical bell, always.

narration_per_round: One. Right. Settle in. We're doing this twelve times.
Two. Left. The first two are the rehearsal.
Six. Left. Halfway through this set.
Seven. Right. Form check. Is the bell vertical? Are you breathing? If not, fix it.
Twelve. Left. Final rep. Make it the cleanest of the twelve.

movements.name: Halo + goblet squat + reverse lunge flow
movements.reps: 1 halo each way + 1 squat + 1 reverse lunge each side. AMRAP 4 min.

blocks.narration: Four minutes of flow. We added the reverse lunge this week. Step back, not forward. The front knee tracks over the front foot. Move continuously.
That is the work. Twelve get-ups, four minutes of flow. The body is learning to be patient under load. Patience is a kind of strength. Rate the session honestly.

Wednesday. Complex day. Five rounds this week, not four. Same movements, more reps on a few of them. Twenty-seven minutes. The good news is you've done four rounds of this. The bad news is the fifth round exists. Let's go, big dog.
Four minutes. Same warm-up, two more squats. Don't tell me you can't tell the difference. Your quads can.

blocks.structure: 5 rounds of the complex. Rest 90s between.
narration_per_round: Round one. Press jumped up to twenty-five pounds. Yes I'm aware. No I'm not sorry. The body needs the load.
Two. Bell stays the same. Your job is to make it move like it weighs less.
Three. Three down, two to go. This is the round where you decide if round five is going to be ugly or honest.
Four. The forearms are loud right now. Tell them they have one more round to wait.
Last round. Round five. We didn't have this round last week. This is bonus. Don't act surprised.

blocks.narration: Three minutes on the rope. Up from two. Find a rhythm and hold it. If you trip, you trip. Pick it up. Keep going.
Wednesday's done. You're halfway through week two and the volume jumped on every session. That's how this works. Rest tomorrow. Real rest. Don't sneak a workout in. I will know. I always know.
Run first. Twenty-two minutes. We added two minutes. Six warm-up, eight rounds of thirty-on thirty-off, eight cooldown. Two more rounds than last week. The body remembers last week, that's the trick.
Six easy. Talk pace. Find the rhythm before we ask it to work.

narration_per_round: One. Hard means hard, not max. Manage it.
Four. Halfway through the hard work.
Eight. Empty the tank on this one.

blocks.narration: Eight minutes easy back. Bring the heart rate down slowly. We've got a bell to lift.

Bell session. Twenty-two. We added two minutes here too. Five rounds instead of four. You're going to feel the run. That's the point. Hybrid training is about lifting tired and running fresh, and learning the difference.

narration_per_round: Last. Right. Round five didn't exist last week. Earn it.

blocks.narration: Hybrid session done. Forty-eight total. You're going to be sore tomorrow. Marcus is taking you on a thirty-five minute long run. Sleep tonight. Hydrate. Eat enough.

workouts.title: Week 2, Day 6. The Long Path, longer.

blocks.narration: Thirty-five minutes today. Five minutes more than last week. Same pace. Easy. The temptation will be to go faster because your legs feel ready. Resist it. The benefit is in the duration, not the speed.

narration_segments.narration: Begin. Nose breathing if you can. Slow the cadence. The pace finds you.
Seven minutes. The body has stopped protesting. Now it cooperates.
Fourteen. Two-fifths through. Watch where the mind goes. Then bring it back to the breath.
Halfway. Marcus Aurelius, again. He wrote that the universe is change, our life is what our thoughts make it. The run is whatever you decide it is in your head. Decide on calm.
Twenty-five. Ten to go. No speeding up.
Thirty. Five left. The discipline is to hold the pace when ego wants you to surge.

blocks.narration: Thirty-five. Done. You ran longer than last week and you did not race. That is what an aerobic engine sounds like being built. Rate it. Tomorrow is Sarge. The grind grows.

Sunday. The grind. Same drill as last week, son. EMOM swings. Same minutes. We're bumping the reps to twelve. Two hundred forty swings instead of two hundred. Twenty percent more work in the same window. That's the deal.
Four minutes. Same as last week. Twelve light swings to finish the warm-up. Same number you'll do at the top of every minute. Practice the count now.

blocks.structure: EMOM x 20. 12 two-hand swings at the top of every minute.
narration_per_round: Minute one. Twelve swings. Same form, more volume. Don't grip the bell to death.
Six. The grip is going to bark at some point. Let it bark. Don't argue back.
Ten. Halfway. Same cue as last week, one breath at the top of next minute before you start.
Twenty. Last minute. Twelve clean ones. Bell empty. Done.

blocks.narration: Two hundred forty swings. End of week two. Foundation phase is two-thirds done. Next week we add a few new tools. Don't get cocky. The patterns you're learning now are the ones you're going to use heavy in eight weeks. Rest up. I'll see you Monday.

weeks.theme: Introduce the clean. Build double-bell awareness.

blocks.narration: Week three. New movement today. The kettlebell clean. The clean is the rack position - bell snug against your forearm, wrist straight, elbow down. Don't swing the bell around the arm. Pull it up and punch through. Twenty-eight minutes.
Three minutes. Single-arm deadlift today - five each side. That's the start position of the clean.

movements.name: Single-arm deadlift
movements.cue: The start of the clean.

narration_per_round: Round one. When you get to the clean, go lighter and slower. Learn the rack first.
Round two. Wrist stays straight in the rack.
Round three. If the bell is banging your forearm, you're swinging it in an arc. Pull straight up, then punch through.
Last round. The clean you finish should look better than the one you started.

movements.name: Clean (right)
movements.cue: Hike back. Pull up like a row. At the top, punch the fist through so the bell sits in the rack.

blocks.narration: Three minutes. Fifteen swings every minute.
Day fifteen. You added a new movement. It's rough now. It'll be clean in two weeks. Rate it honest.
Two things today. Twelve get-ups at the same weight. And the double-bell front rack carry. Two bells in the rack, walking. Your core will speak to you in a language it has never used before.
Four minutes. Bird dogs wake the anti-rotation pattern the carries depend on.

blocks.structure: 12 get-ups alternating, then 4 x 30s front rack carry
narration_per_round: One. Right. The rack position for the carry starts here.
Seven. Right. Carries start after twelve.
Twelve. Left. Get-ups complete. Carries in thirty seconds.

movements.name: Double front rack carry
movements.cue: Both bells in the rack. Walk tall. Ribs down. Don't let the weight pull you into extension.

blocks.narration: Four minutes. Standard flow.

movements.name: Halo + goblet squat + reverse lunge flow

blocks.narration: Twelve get-ups. Four rack carries. The core is learning what a loaded spine feels like. Rate the session.

workouts.title: Week 3, Day 3. Clean in the complex.

blocks.narration: Alright big dog. The clean joins the party. Five rounds, but we're swapping the row for clean-to-press. It's a harder chain. The clean loads the press.
Four minutes. Standard. A few slow cleans at the end with no weight.

narration_per_round: Round one. Take the clean-press slow. This is a skill round.
Three. The clean should start connecting with the press.
Four. If the press is failing, the clean is the problem. Fix the rack.

movements.name: Clean + press (right)
movements.cue: Clean to rack, pause, press.

blocks.narration: Three minutes rope.
Done. The clean-to-press is a chain you'll use for the next nine weeks. Rate it honest.

workouts.title: Week 3, Day 5. Double day — Tempo added.

blocks.narration: Friday double. Adding a tempo block to the run today. After the intervals, four minutes at sustainable discomfort. Then the bell session.
Six minutes easy.

blocks.structure: 6 rounds: 30s hard / 30s easy, then 4 min tempo, then KB 5 rounds
narration_per_round: Six. Last interval. Now four minutes tempo.

blocks.narration: Cooldown jog, then five rounds of clean-press and swings after rest.
Hybrid session done. Rate it.
Thirty-five minutes. Same as last week. We don't add time every week. Sometimes we hold distance and improve the relationship to the pace.

narration_segments.narration: Eight minutes. The first resistance is gone.
Halfway. Notice where the tension lives. Let it go.
Ten to go. Hold the pace exactly.

blocks.narration: Done. Same time as last week. Different relationship to it. That is progress.

workouts.title: Week 3, Day 7. The Grind. Bell up.

blocks.narration: Sunday grind. Same twenty minutes. Same twelve reps per minute. Try the 30-pounder if the 25 has started to feel light. Ego doesn't survive twenty minutes of EMOM.
Four minutes. Same prep.

blocks.structure: EMOM x 20. 12 two-hand swings per minute.

blocks.narration: Two hundred forty swings. Three weeks in. Rate it. Next week Foundation closes.

workouts.title: Week 4, Day 1. Double front squat enters.

blocks.narration: Week four. Last week of Foundation phase. New tool: the double-bell front squat. Two twenty-pound bells in the rack. The racks want to pull you forward. Chest up. Elbows up.
Three minutes. Practice holding both bells in the rack before we load it.

narration_per_round: Round one. Double front squat is new today. Light and slow.
Two. The bells should feel more familiar in the rack. Elbows don't drop.
Three. Press work is at twenty-five now.
Four. Last round. Foundation closes after this week.

movements.name: Double front rack squat
movements.cue: Both bells in the rack. Chest up. Elbows up. Squat between the bells.

blocks.narration: Three minutes. Fifteen swings per minute.
Week four, day one. You squatted with two bells in the rack today. Foundation phase ends Sunday.
The carry changes today. Suitcase carry - one bell held at your side. The challenge is not to lean toward the bell. The anti-lean is the work.
Four minutes. Bird dogs are more important today than any other warm-up.

blocks.structure: 12 get-ups alternating, then 4 x 30s suitcase carry each side
narration_per_round: Twelve. Left. Get-ups complete. Suitcase carries. Don't lean.

movements.name: Suitcase carry (right)
movements.cue: Bell in right hand at side. Walk tall. Don't lean right. The obliques hold you straight.

blocks.narration: Four minutes flow. Last Tuesday of Foundation phase.

movements.name: Halo + goblet squat + reverse lunge flow

blocks.narration: The get-up and the carry teach the same lesson: stable position under load. Rate the session. Build phase starts Monday.

workouts.title: Week 4, Day 3. The full Foundation complex.

blocks.narration: Last Wednesday of Foundation. Six movements total. Five rounds. This is the densest Foundation session. Twenty-nine minutes.
Four minutes. Standard.

narration_per_round: Three. The third of five separates the session into before and after.
Five. Last one. Foundation phase ends Sunday.

blocks.narration: Three minutes.
Foundation's last Wednesday. Rate it.

workouts.title: Week 4, Day 5. Double day — 5 min tempo.

blocks.narration: Last Foundation double. Run goes to 8 intervals plus 5 minutes tempo. KB stays five rounds. Forty-eight total.
Six easy.

blocks.structure: 8 rounds: 30s hard / 30s easy, then 5 min tempo, then KB 5 rounds
narration_per_round: Eight. Last interval. Now five minutes tempo.

blocks.narration: Cooldown, then bell. Five rounds after rest.
Foundation double day complete. Rest tomorrow. Sarge closes Foundation Sunday with 252 swings.

workouts.title: Week 4, Day 6. Foundation's last long run.

blocks.narration: Last long run of Foundation phase. Thirty-five minutes at a pace you could sustain for an hour. Showing up for the sixth session of a heavy week is the test.

narration_segments.narration: Begin. This is the final Foundation run.
Ten minutes. The body has settled.
Halfway. Epictetus: it is not what happens to you but how you react that matters.

blocks.narration: Done. Tomorrow Sarge. Foundation ends. Rate it.
Last session of Foundation phase, son. Twenty-one minutes. Twelve swings per minute. Two hundred fifty-two total. Three more than last week. It's not a PR attempt. It's a close-out.
Four minutes. Last Foundation warm-up.

blocks.structure: EMOM x 21. 12 two-hand swings per minute = 252 swings.
narration_per_round: Twenty-one. Final minute of Foundation phase. Twelve swings. Bell down.

blocks.narration: Two hundred fifty-two swings. Foundation phase complete. Four weeks. Twenty-four sessions. Build phase starts Monday. Heavier. Longer. More complex. Rest today.

weeks.theme: Build phase begins. EMOMs lengthen. Doubles arrive.

workouts.title: Week 5, Day 1. Build begins. Double cleans.

blocks.narration: Build phase. Sessions go to twenty-eight, twenty-nine minutes. Double cleans today - two bells at once. You've got the single clean. This is just both hands doing the same thing at the same time.
Three minutes. Two light cleans at the end to practice the simultaneous pull.

narration_per_round: Round one. Double clean is new. Two bells, same timing. Pull both straight up.
Two. The double clean should start to sync.
Three. Press load crept to twenty-five on both sides.

movements.name: Double clean
movements.cue: Both bells, both hands, same timing. Pull up, punch through, rack.

blocks.narration: Three minutes. Fifteen swings. Same drill.
Build phase, day one. You doubled the clean. Rate it honest.
Fourteen get-ups today. Seven each side. We add two. The weight stays at twenty pounds. More reps at the same weight is more time practicing the pattern.
Four minutes. Same preparation.

narration_per_round: Fourteen. Left. Final rep. Make it deliberate.

movements.name: Turkish get-up
movements.cue: Fourteen reps. Same cues. Eyes on the bell going up. Packed shoulder throughout.

blocks.narration: Four minutes. Move continuously.

movements.name: Halo + goblet squat + reverse lunge flow

blocks.narration: Fourteen get-ups. More reps at the same weight before we add weight. Rate the session.
Build phase Wednesday. The complex now includes double bells on the squat. Two twenty-pounders. Five rounds, tighter rest windows. Twenty-nine minutes.
Four minutes. Standard. A few double cleans at the end.

narration_per_round: Round one. Rest is shorter now. Seventy-five seconds between rounds.
Two. The double squat demands more of your upper back than you expect.
Three. Halfway. The conditioning gap between Foundation and Build is visible right now.
Five. Last round of Build's first Wednesday.

blocks.narration: Three minutes rope.
Done. Double bells are in the complex now. They stay. Rate it.
Build phase double. The tempo intervals get longer today. Three rounds of three minutes hard. Nine minutes of tempo work after the intervals. Fifty total minutes.
Six easy.

blocks.structure: 6 rounds 30s/30s + 3x3min tempo with 90s recovery, then KB 5 rounds
narration_per_round: One through six intervals. Then three-minute tempos. Three of them. Then KB.

blocks.narration: Cool down. Rest. Five rounds of double clean, swing, squat.
Fifty minutes. Build phase double. Rate it.
Build phase adds three minutes to the long run. Thirty-eight. Easy. The aerobic base is a slow infrastructure project. This session is another brick.

narration_segments.narration: Ten minutes. Past the start-up resistance.

blocks.narration: Thirty-eight. Done. Build phase is running longer and lifting heavier. Rate it.

workouts.title: Week 5, Day 7. Swing and snatch mix begins.

blocks.narration: Sunday grind changes this week. Swing-heavy EMOM but at minute ten you'll do five single-arm swings per side. Think of them as the start of the snatch. Hip snap is the same. The bell just travels higher.
Four minutes. Add single-arm swings at the end. Five each side with the light bell.

blocks.structure: EMOM x 22. Minutes 1-9: 12 two-hand swings. Minutes 10-22 alternate 10 swings and 5 single-arm swings each side.
narration_per_round: Nine. Last two-hand minute. Next minute changes.
Ten. Five single-arm right, five single-arm left.

blocks.narration: You met the single-arm swing. Next week the bell goes overhead. Rate it.

weeks.theme: Snatch enters. The single-arm swing as bridge.

blocks.narration: Week six. The single-arm swing is in your toolkit. Today we use it in the strength session. Form cue: the free hand makes a fist and swings in opposition.
Three minutes. Single-arm swings in the warm-up.

movements.name: Single-arm swing (right)
movements.cue: Free hand fisted, swings in opposition.

narration_per_round: Round one. Single-arm swing is in. Keep the free hand fisted.
Two. The double work gets cleaner because of single-arm practice.
Three. Press at twenty-five. Row at twenty-five.

blocks.narration: Three minutes. Fifteen single-arm swings alternating.
Single-arm swing is the bridge to the snatch. Rate it.

Today we introduce the snatch. Ten get-ups. Then snatch practice. The snatch is the single-arm swing that goes overhead. The bell travels in a vertical path. At the top, punch up through the handle. Do not muscle it overhead.
Four minutes. Extra time on single-arm swings before the snatch.

blocks.structure: 10 get-ups, then 5+5 snatch practice AMRAP 8 min

movements.name: Snatch
movements.cue: Single-arm swing. At shoulder height, punch up through the handle. Bell flips over the fist. Lock out overhead.

narration_per_round: One through ten get-ups. Then eight minutes snatch practice. Use the lightest bell.

blocks.narration: Three minutes. Easy flow.
The snatch is not easy. It took six weeks to get here. Rate the session.
Single-arm swings are in the complex now. Five rounds. The single-arm swing replaces one of the two-hand swing sets.
Four minutes. Standard. A few single-arm swings at the end.

narration_per_round: Round one. Single-arm swing is different. Respect the free hand.

blocks.narration: Three minutes rope.
Done. Single-arm is in. Snatch is next. Rate it.
Double day. Run with snatch skill work after intervals today. Not conditioning yet — skill work. Five snatches each side. Then KB with single-arm swings.
Six easy.

blocks.structure: 8 rounds 30s/30s + 3x3min tempo + snatch skill + KB 5 rounds
narration_per_round: Eight intervals. Three tempos. Then KB.

blocks.narration: Cooldown. KB after rest.
Single-arm work is in the double day. Rate it.
Forty minutes. Two minutes longer than last week but psychologically different. Forty feels longer than thirty-eight. We are slowly moving that threshold upward.

narration_segments.narration: Twenty. Halfway. The second half is always shorter in the mind.

blocks.narration: Forty minutes. Done. Rate the session.
Grind day changes. Fifteen rounds. Odd minutes: ten two-hand swings. Even minutes: five snatches per side with the lightest bell. Keep it light. Patterning, not weight.
Four minutes. Snatch practice without weight.

blocks.structure: EMOM x 15. Odd: 10 two-hand swings. Even: 5 snatches right + 5 snatches left.
narration_per_round: Two. Five snatches each side. Bell stays vertical.
Four. Snatches. Punch up through the handle.

blocks.narration: Hundred fifty swings and seventy snatches. The snatch is in the grind. Rate it.
Density week. E2MOM today - every two minutes on the minute. Two movements per round. The time left after you finish is your rest. Faster you move, more rest you get.
Three minutes.

blocks.structure: E2MOM x 12 rounds. Each round: double clean x5 + double squat x5.

movements.name: Double clean
movements.cue: Both bells simultaneous.

movements.name: Double front rack squat
movements.cue: Rack the bells from the clean.

narration_per_round: Round one. Five cleans, five squats. Rest what's left of two minutes.

blocks.narration: Three minutes. Clean + press ladder. 1 right, 1 left, 2, 2, 3, 3.
E2MOM is a density tool. You did more work in less structure. Rate it.
Fourteen get-ups. Then a snatch ladder. One right, one left. Two right, two left. Up to five. Rest. Down to one. The ladder teaches volume management over fatigue.
Four minutes. More snatch prep.

blocks.structure: 14 get-ups, then snatch ladder 1-2-3-4-5-4-3-2-1 each side

movements.name: Snatch ladder
movements.cue: Same cues. Vertical path. Punch up.

narration_per_round: One through fourteen get-ups. Then ladder. One right, one left. Two. Three. Four. Five. Down.

blocks.narration: Three minutes. Easy.
Ladder work teaches volume management. Rate the session.
E2MOM Wednesday. Every two minutes: swing, squat, clean-press, row. Whatever time's left in the window is your rest. Welcome to density.
Four minutes.

narration_per_round: Round one. Move through. Rest what's left.

blocks.narration: Five minutes. Up from three.
E2MOM means density. Rest is earned. Rate it.
Four tempo intervals today. Twelve minutes of threshold running total. After the intervals and cooldown, KB session runs E2MOM format. Fifty-two minutes total.
Six easy.

narration_per_round: Eight intervals. Four tempos. Then KB E2MOM.

blocks.narration: Cooldown. KB after rest.
Density week double. Fifty-two minutes. Rate it.

workouts.title: Week 7, Day 6. Forty minutes — hold pace.

blocks.narration: Forty minutes. Same as last week. The same distance after a density week feels different. The body is more fatigued. Hold the pace anyway. This is the adaptation stress.

narration_segments.narration: Begin. Notice the legs. They remember this week.
Ten to go. This is where the week shows up.

blocks.narration: Forty done. Next week is the last Build week. The test comes Sunday.
Twenty-minute ladder today. Odd minutes: ten two-hand swings. Even minutes: snatch ladder - one right, one left. Two. Three. Back down.
Four minutes. Snatch practice at light weight.

blocks.structure: EMOM x 20. Odd: 10 swings. Even: snatch ladder progresses over 10 even minutes.

blocks.narration: Density week grind. Rate it. Next week ends with the Build test.
Last Monday of Build phase. E2MOM structure. You know the drill. Every two minutes, work the complex, rest what's left. Thirty minutes.
Three minutes.

blocks.structure: E2MOM x 12 rounds — heavier than week 7
narration_per_round: Round one. Heavier if you've been progressing.

blocks.narration: Three minutes. Two-hand swings AMRAP. Count your reps.
Eight weeks of Monday strength work. Rate it.
Last technical Tuesday of Build phase. Fourteen get-ups. Then five sets of five snatches each side. Not a snatch test. Skill consolidation before Forge.
Four minutes.

movements.name: Snatch
movements.cue: Five sets. Fifty total snatches. Keep the bell close.

narration_per_round: Get-ups one through fourteen. Then snatch sets.

blocks.narration: Three minutes.

movements.name: Halo + goblet squat + reverse lunge flow

blocks.narration: Fifty snatches. Pattern is becoming a movement. Sunday is the Build test. Rate it.

workouts.title: Week 8, Day 3. Dense complex, peak Build.

blocks.narration: Last Wednesday of Build phase. E2MOM complex. Snatch is in the conditioning block. Brief sets under fatigue. That's what Forge demands.
Four minutes.

blocks.structure: E2MOM x 10 rounds plus 4 min snatch practice
narration_per_round: Round one. Snatch is in. Three each side.

blocks.narration: Five minutes. Last conditioning finisher of Build phase.
Done. Build phase ends Sunday. Show up.
Last Build double. Fifty minutes. Run: eight intervals, four tempos. KB: E2MOM with snatch. If you finish clean, you're ready for Forge.
Six easy.

blocks.structure: 8 rounds 30s/30s + 4x3min tempo + KB E2MOM with snatch
narration_per_round: Eight intervals. Four tempos. Then E2MOM KB.

blocks.narration: Cooldown. KB after rest.
Fifty minutes. Build double done. Sunday is the mini-test. Come fresh.
Forty minutes. Same distance. Different instruction for the last five: if your legs are under you, run ten to fifteen seconds per mile faster. Not a sprint. An uptick.

blocks.structure: 35 min easy, last 5 min at moderate effort

narration_segments.narration: The final five begins in five minutes.
Here. Shift the effort slightly. Not a sprint. A gear up.

blocks.narration: Forty done with a gear shift. Tomorrow is the Build test. Rest today.

workouts.title: Week 8, Day 7. Build closes. AMRAP test.

blocks.narration: Build test. Ten minutes. AMRAP. The complex: five two-hand swings, three double cleans, two clean-and-press each side. Count your rounds. Write the number down. This is your Build baseline. In four weeks at the end of Forge, you'll test again.
Four minutes. Get warm enough for full intensity.

blocks.structure: AMRAP 10 min — 5 swings + 3 double cleans + 2 clean-press each side

blocks.narration: Ten minutes. Build test complete. Write down your rounds. Forge phase starts Monday. That number goes up in four weeks. I guarantee it.

Forge phase. The fifty-pound bell is in the room. We use it for swings and goblet squats. The double bells and presses stay at twenty-five. Treat the fifty like a new officer. Respect it first. Thirty minutes.
Three minutes. Warm up with the light bell before the fifty.

movements.name: Two-hand swing
movements.cue: The fifty is heavier. The hinge has to be deeper. The hip snap sharper.

movements.name: Goblet squat
movements.cue: Chest up harder. The fifty wants to drag you forward.

narration_per_round: Round one. First round with the fifty on swings. Drive the hips harder.
Two. The goblet squat at fifty is different.
Three. Press and double work stays at twenty-five. More fatigue.
Four. Last round. Forge phase, first Monday.

blocks.narration: Three minutes. Ten swings per minute. With the fifty.
The fifty-pound bell is in the program now. It stays. Rate it honest.
Today we move the get-up to twenty-five pounds. Fourteen reps. Five more pounds. The get-up reveals everything. More weight reveals more.
Four minutes. One get-up each side with the twenty first.

movements.name: Turkish get-up
movements.cue: Twenty-five pounds. The packed shoulder is critical. Move slowly. Each position is a checkpoint.

narration_per_round: One through fourteen. Twenty-five pounds. The shoulder talks louder now. Listen.

blocks.narration: Four minutes snatch practice. The get-up weight went up. The snatch did not.

movements.name: Snatch
movements.reps: 5 x 5 each side, rest as needed

blocks.narration: Twenty-five-pound get-ups. Rate the session.
Forge Wednesday. The swing goes to fifty. The rest of the complex stays at twenty-five. Five rounds, E2MOM. The fifty-pound swing changes the metabolic demand.
Four minutes. Swings at light bell to groove pattern before the fifty.

narration_per_round: Round one. Swings go heavy. Everything else stays at twenty-five.

blocks.narration: Five minutes.
Forge phase Wednesday one. The fifty is in the conditioning. Rate it.
Forge double. The run adds threshold intervals today. Four times four minutes. Four minutes is long enough that you can't sprint through it. Find the pace at the edge of sustainable. Then hold it.
Six easy.

blocks.structure: 4 x 4min threshold intervals with 2min recovery, then KB 4 rounds
narration_per_round: Threshold one. Four minutes hard but not sprint.

blocks.narration: Cooldown. KB E2MOM after rest.
Threshold intervals are the hardest run work in the program. Rate it honest.
Forge phase adds two minutes to the long run. Forty-two. Easy pace. The body is adapting to heavier loads. The long run is recovery work dressed as effort.

narration_segments.narration: Begin. Forge phase adds time everywhere.

blocks.narration: Forty-two done. Rate it.
Forge grind. Fifteen rounds. The fifty-pound bell. Eight swings per minute. One hundred twenty swings. That's sixty fewer than the Foundation grind but twenty pounds heavier. The math is different.
Four minutes. Warm-up with the fifty is not optional.

blocks.structure: EMOM x 15. 8 two-hand swings per minute at 50lb.

blocks.narration: One hundred twenty swings at fifty pounds. Forge phase one. Rate it.
The double bells go to twenty-five pounds today. Two twenty-fives in the clean. Two twenty-fives in the squat. Fifty pounds of iron in the rack simultaneously. Don't collapse forward.
Three minutes. Warm up the double at twenty before twenty-five.

movements.name: Double clean
movements.cue: Two twenty-fives. Simultaneous. Elbows higher.

movements.name: Double front rack squat
movements.cue: Fifty pounds in the rack. Chest up hard.

narration_per_round: Round one. Double twenty-five. The clean rack feels different at this weight.
Two. The squat loads your anterior chain hard.
Three. Presses stay at twenty-five single bell.
Four. Last round. Ten weeks in.

blocks.narration: Three minutes. Ten swings. Fifty pounds.
Double twenty-fives are in. Rate it honest.
Sixteen get-ups today. Eight each side. Twenty-five pounds. The goal this week: notice the quality of the sixteenth rep relative to the first. If it deteriorates, that is the work.
Four minutes. Two get-ups at twenty to start.

blocks.structure: 16 get-ups alternating at 25lb, then 3x10 snatches each side

movements.name: Turkish get-up
movements.cue: Sixteen. The sixteenth should look like the first.

narration_per_round: One through sixteen. Then three sets of ten snatches each side.

blocks.narration: Three minutes.
Sixteen get-ups at twenty-five. Thirty snatches. Rate the session.

The Forge complex. Double clean, double squat, single press, snatch. The most demanding complex we've run. E2MOM, ten rounds. The snatch is at the end, so you'll be doing it fatigued. That's intentional.
Four minutes. The full movement chain at lighter weight.

narration_per_round: Round one. Double clean, double squat, press right, press left, snatch right, snatch left.
Five. Halfway. The snatch under fatigue is honest.

blocks.narration: Five minutes. The complex earned it.
The Forge complex. Rate it.
Forge double. Forty-five minute run with a ten-minute threshold block in the middle. Not at the end — in the middle. You'll threshold, recover, then run another twenty minutes easy. Then KB.
Seven easy minutes.

blocks.structure: 18 easy + 10 threshold + 17 easy, then KB E2MOM
narration_per_round: Eighteen easy. Then ten minutes threshold. Then seventeen easy. Rest. Then KB E2MOM.

blocks.narration: Rest after run. KB E2MOM after rest.
Forty-five minute run plus KB. Forge pace. Rate it.
Forty-five minutes. Three minutes longer. The aerobic base continues to expand. If you can't breathe through your nose, you're going too fast.

narration_segments.narration: Ten to go. The body wants to rush. Tell it no.

blocks.narration: Forty-five. Done. Peak run week approaches. Rate it.
Sunday is a snatch test now. Twenty minutes. EMOM. Ten snatches per minute, alternating sides. Two hundred total. Manage the grip. The snatch test is the standard of kettlebell conditioning.
Four minutes. Snatch prep thoroughly.

blocks.structure: EMOM x 20. 10 snatches per minute alternating sides.

movements.name: Snatch
movements.cue: Manage the grip. Bell stays close. Vertical path. At the top, punch up and lock out.

narration_per_round: One. Ten snatches. Five right five left.

blocks.narration: Two hundred snatches. Rate it honest. Next week is peak volume. Then taper. Then the final test.

weeks.theme: Peak volume. The week that earns the crown.

blocks.narration: Peak volume week. Every session is at maximum. You don't skip this week. You don't go easy. Soreness is not broken. Fatigue is not broken. Show up and do the work.
Three minutes. Fast.

narration_per_round: Round one. Five rounds. Peak volume.

blocks.narration: Three minutes. Ten swings. Fifty pounds.
Peak Monday done. Rate it. Six more sessions this week.

workouts.title: Week 11, Day 2. Sixteen get-ups at twenty-five.

blocks.narration: Sixteen get-ups at twenty-five pounds. Then a snatch ladder. Peak week means every session has more surrounding it. Hold the standard.
Four minutes.

blocks.structure: 16 get-ups at 25lb, then 2x snatch ladders 1-2-3-4-5 each side

movements.name: Snatch ladder
movements.reps: 2 x (1-2-3-4-5 each side), rest as needed
movements.cue: Two ladders. Ninety snatches total.

narration_per_round: One through sixteen. Then two snatch ladders.

blocks.narration: Three minutes flow.

movements.name: Halo + goblet squat + reverse lunge flow

blocks.narration: Sixteen get-ups and ninety snatches. Peak Tuesday. Rate it.

Peak conditioning Wednesday. The Forge complex. E2MOM, twelve rounds. Thirty minutes. The snatch is in there under fatigue. Peak week means you don't reduce reps because you're tired. You find the pace.
Four minutes.

narration_per_round: Round one. Twelve rounds of the Forge complex.

blocks.narration: Five minutes. Peak week.
Peak Wednesday done. Rate it. Double day Friday.
Fifty-five minutes. Peak week double. Run: twenty easy, ten threshold, fifteen easy. Then KB E2MOM Forge complex, twelve rounds. Hardest double in the program.
Seven easy.

blocks.structure: 20 easy + 10 threshold + 15 easy + KB E2MOM x12
narration_per_round: Twenty easy. Ten threshold. Fifteen easy. Rest. Then KB E2MOM.

blocks.narration: Rest after run. KB after rest.
Fifty-five minutes. Peak double. Rate it.

Fifty minutes. The longest run in this program. Easy pace. Non-negotiable. The body is at peak load this week. The long run is stress recovery, not additional stress. Run slower than you think you need to.

narration_segments.narration: Five minutes. Hold pace. Don't surge.

blocks.narration: Fifty minutes. Longest run in Forge40. Rate it. Tomorrow is the peak grind.

Peak grind. Twenty-five minutes. Minutes one through ten: eight swings at fifty. Minutes eleven through twenty: five snatches per side at twenty. Minutes twenty-one through twenty-five: eight swings at fifty. Show up for all twenty-five.
Four minutes. Both the swing and snatch are in today.

blocks.structure: EMOM x 25: minutes 1-10 eight heavy swings, 11-20 five snatches per side, 21-25 eight heavy swings.
narration_per_round: Ten. Swing block done. Snatch block begins.
Twenty. Snatch block done. Swings come back.

blocks.narration: Twenty-five minutes. Peak grind complete. Week eleven is done. One week remains. Taper starts Monday. Rest more than you think you need to.

Week twelve. Test week. Volume drops thirty percent. The taper is not weakness. It's the realization of all the work you put in. The body needs these days to peak for Sunday. Move well. Don't go hard. Twenty-two minutes.
Three minutes.

narration_per_round: Round one. Three rounds. Technique focus. Every rep crisp.
Two. Same weights. Half the volume.
Three. Final Monday session. Make it clean.

blocks.narration: Two minutes easy swings to flush the pattern.
Taper Monday done. Rate it. Three more sessions before Sunday. Rest is training this week.
Ten get-ups. Twenty-five pounds. The last technical Tuesday. Not adding anything new. Arriving at Sunday with all the patterns fresh and rested.
Four minutes. Unhurried.

movements.name: Turkish get-up
movements.cue: Ten reps. The same attention you brought to the first session. The same packed shoulder. The same vertical bell.

narration_per_round: One through ten. Last Tuesday of the program. Make each rep deliberate.

blocks.narration: Three minutes. Easy flow.
Ten clean get-ups. You have been doing get-ups since week one. They are part of you now. Sunday is coming.
Last Wednesday. Taper. Three rounds of the Forge complex. Not five, not ten. Three. Move through it with intent. Sunday is the test. Today is the final preparation.
Four minutes.

narration_per_round: Round one. Three rounds. Taper week.
Two. Move well. Not fast, not heavy. Well.
Three. Last Wednesday. Final preparation round.

blocks.narration: Three minutes easy rope.
Last Wednesday done. Rest tomorrow. Easy Friday. Rest Saturday. Show up Sunday ready.
Easy double. Thirty minutes total. Twenty easy run. Ten minutes light KB. This is not a training day. It's a maintenance flush. Save everything for Sunday.
Five easy.

blocks.structure: 20 min easy run + 10 min light KB
narration_per_round: Easy run. Twenty minutes. No intervals. No tempo. Then ten minutes of light KB.

blocks.narration: Easy cooldown.
Easy double done. Rest Saturday. Sleep. Eat well.

workouts.title: Week 12, Day 6. Thirty minutes. Last long run.

blocks.narration: Thirty minutes. Easy. This is the last long run. We do not add time in test week. The aerobic base is built. Today is maintenance. Arrive at Sunday rested.

narration_segments.narration: Begin. The last long run of the program.
Halfway. Marcus Aurelius: You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength. Tomorrow you will find out what you built.

blocks.narration: Last long run. Twelve weeks of running. You've built a real aerobic base. Rest today. Tomorrow is the test. Everything you've done has prepared you for it.

This is it, son. Twelve weeks. The Forge40 benchmark. Thirty minutes. Maximum effort. The complex: five two-hand swings at the heaviest bell you've used. Three double cleans. Two clean-and-press each side. One get-up each side. That's one round. AMRAP thirty minutes. Write your score. Compare it to Sunday week eight. That gap is the twelve weeks.
Six minutes. Full warm-up. The test requires full preparation.

blocks.structure: AMRAP 30 min — 5 swings + 3 double cleans + 2 clean-press each side + 1 TGU each side

movements.name: Two-hand swing
movements.cue: Maximum effort.

narration_per_round: Go. Thirty minutes. Five swings, three double cleans, two presses each side, one get-up each side.
Fifteen minutes. Halfway. Find your pace.
Twenty-five minutes. Five left. Everything you have.

blocks.narration: Thirty minutes. Done. Write the number down. Compare it to week eight. That difference is twelve weeks of Foundation, Build, and Forge. That is the work. Rate this session honest. The crown was never given. It was built rep by rep, session by session, week by week. It is yours. You have earned it. Dismissed.
